dc41.title: Retro board: undo / redo
dc41.summary: A sticky-note retro board already adds, edits and deletes notes. Add an undo/redo history with buttons and Ctrl/Cmd+Z.
dc41.brief:
Pinboard is a team retro board. App.tsx has Header, Toolbar, NoteCard and App. You can already add a note (in the picked color), type in it, and delete it. getBoard() in api.ts loads the notes after a random 0.3–0.9 s.

Product wants undo and redo. Read components/IconButton.tsx (use it for the new buttons) and utils/id.ts first.

The interesting decision is the shape of the state: right now it is one notes array. Undo needs the old versions too.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4–5. Change: cap history at 20 (~24 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan out loud · 7–24 Core · 24–31 change + Next · 31–35 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Every change to the notes becomes a snapshot. I'll replace notes with one state object { past, present, future } so the three always change together. Add and delete call commit(next): push present onto past, set the new present, clear future. Undo pops past into present and pushes the old present onto future; redo is the mirror. I'll write those as pure functions (h) => newH so I can pass them straight to setHistory, and the keydown effect doesn't need any dependencies.

Typing is the tricky part: one undo per keystroke would be awful. I'll update present without a history entry while typing, remember a snapshot on focus in a useRef, and on blur commit that snapshot to past if the notes changed. Can-undo / can-redo are derived from the array lengths."
requirements: Toolbar gets Undo and Redo buttons (use IconButton). Undo is disabled when there is nothing to undo, Redo when there is nothing to redo. Loading the board is not an undoable step
Adding and deleting a note can be undone and redone. A deleted note comes back in the same position. Doing a new action after an undo clears the redo stack
Editing a note's text is one undo step per edit (commit when the note loses focus), not one step per keystroke
Ctrl/Cmd+Z undoes and Shift+Ctrl/Cmd+Z redoes. While the cursor is in a note's textarea the shortcut is left to the browser (native text undo)
The keydown listener is added once in an effect and removed in the cleanup; no stale state (undo twice quickly must undo two steps)

change.title: Cap the history at 20
change.html:
"On long retros the history grows forever and we keep every snapshot in memory."

  • Keep at most 20 undo steps. The oldest step is dropped when a 21st is added.
  • Show a small meter next to the buttons: "3 / 20" (undo steps available / max).

Hint: one .slice(-20) in the right place. Check that every path that pushes to past uses it.

hints: State shape: type History = { past: Note[][]; present: Note[]; future: Note[][] }. The notes you render are history.present.
Write pure helpers outside the component: function undoHistory(h: History): History { ... }. Then setHistory(undoHistory) works from a button and from a keydown listener with [] deps.
Commit: return { past: [...h.past, h.present], present: next, future: [] };. Undo: take the last item of past, put the old present at the front of future.
Keyboard: if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key.toLowerCase() === "z"). With Shift held, e.key is uppercase "Z", hence toLowerCase(). Search: "mdn KeyboardEvent metaKey".
Skip the shortcut while typing: const t = e.target as HTMLElement; if (t.tagName === "TEXTAREA") return;
Text edits: onFocus stores editStart.current = history.present; typing does setHistory((h) => ({ ...h, present: next })); onBlur pushes editStart.current onto past if h.present !== editStart.current.
rubric: Chose a single history object (past / present / future) and explained why
Undo / redo / commit are pure and never mutate arrays
Buttons' disabled states are derived from stack lengths, not stored
Keydown listener cleaned up; updater form avoids stale closures
Typing does not create one history entry per keystroke
Cap applied to every path that grows the past stack
Talked through edge cases (redo cleared after a new action, load not undoable)

dc42.title: Photo feed: infinite scroll
dc42.summary: A dark photo feed only shows the first page. Load the next page automatically when the user nears the bottom, using IntersectionObserver.
dc42.brief:
Aperture is a photo community. App.tsx has TopBar, Feed and App; cards are rendered by components/PhotoCard.tsx, and components/Spinner.tsx is a loading row you should reuse. The feed scrolls inside its own container (.feed-scroll), not the window.

getPhotos(cursor) returns { photos, nextCursor } after 0.5–1.1 s. nextCursor is null on the last page (40 photos in total). It logs every request to the console, so you can see duplicate loads.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4. Change: "Back to top" button (~24 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan · 7–24 Core · 24–31 change · 31–35 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"State in Feed: photos, nextCursor (start at 0, null means done) and loading. I'll put an empty sentinel div after the last card and observe it with an IntersectionObserver whose root is the scroll container, not the viewport. When it intersects and nothing is in flight, I fetch the next page and append.

The observer callback is a closure, so for the in-flight guard I'll use a useRef; a state value would be stale inside it. The effect depends on nextCursor: each page recreates the observer, and if the sentinel is still visible it fires again, which fills tall screens. When nextCursor is null the effect just doesn't observe, and I show "You're all caught up". Cleanup disconnects."
requirements: The first page loads on mount (no button). When the user scrolls near the bottom of .feed-scroll, the next page is fetched with the previous nextCursor and appended. Use an IntersectionObserver on a sentinel element with the scroll container as root (not a scroll event)
While a page is loading, a loading row ("Loading more photos…", reuse Spinner) shows at the bottom of the list
No duplicate requests: scrolling up and down while a request is in flight never starts a second one, and no photo appears twice
At the end (nextCursor === null) the observer stops and the list ends with "You're all caught up · 40 photos". The observer is disconnected on unmount

change.title: Back to top
change.html:
"After 40 photos, getting back to the top is painful."

  • Once the feed is scrolled more than 800px, show a floating pill "↑ Back to top" centered at the bottom of the feed.
  • Clicking it smooth-scrolls the feed container to the top; the button disappears when back near the top.

Search: "mdn element scrollTo behavior smooth". The button needs a position: relative parent that does not scroll.

hints: You need two refs: scrollRef on .feed-scroll (the observer root) and sentinelRef on an empty div after the cards.
Search: "mdn IntersectionObserver root rootMargin". new IntersectionObserver(cb, { root: scrollRef.current, rootMargin: "0px 0px 300px 0px" }) starts loading 300px before the end.
Why a ref for the in-flight flag? The callback was created when the effect ran; a loading state value inside it is frozen at that moment. inFlight.current is always current.
Effect shape: useEffect(() => { if (nextCursor === null) return; const obs = new IntersectionObserver(...); obs.observe(sentinelRef.current); return () => { obs.disconnect(); }; }, [nextCursor]);

Inside the callback: if (!entries[0].isIntersecting || inFlight.current) return; inFlight.current = true; getPhotos(cursor).then((page) => { setPhotos((prev) => [...prev, ...page.photos]); setNextCursor(page.nextCursor); inFlight.current = false; });
rubric: Observer root is the feed's scroll container, not the window
In-flight guard explained (ref vs stale state in a closure)
Appends with the updater form; never duplicates
Stops cleanly at the end and disconnects on cleanup
Loading and end states are separate decisions above the return
Back-to-top derived from scrollTop with a threshold; smooth scroll on the container
Mentioned the alternative (scroll listener + math) and why the observer is better

notes: absolute · bottom 20 · centered · h 36 · pill · 13/700 · shadow 0 6 20

dc43.title: Playlist: drag to reorder
dc43.summary: Reorder a playlist with HTML5 drag and drop plus accessible Move up/down buttons, then save the order to the API.
dc43.brief:
Sunday Slow Mornings is a playlist page. App.tsx has PlaylistHeader, TrackRow, TrackList and App. getPlaylist() takes 0.4–1.0 s; savePlaylistOrder(trackIds) takes 0.6–1.2 s. utils/time.ts has formatDuration and formatTotal; components/Cover.tsx draws album art.

The tracks currently come straight from playlist.tracks. To reorder them you'll need your own copy in state.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4. Change: durations + "Unsaved changes" (~24 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan · 7–24 Core · 24–31 change · 31–35 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"I'll keep tracks in state (copied from the API) and one pure helper moveItem(list, from, to) that both drag and drop and the buttons call, so there's one code path. For drag: dragId in state on dragstart; on dragover I preventDefault (or drop never fires) and work out before / after from the mouse Y against the row's midpoint, stored as dropTarget to draw the line. On drop, convert to an index, remembering that removing the dragged row shifts later indexes by one.

Buttons are the accessible path: "Move X up / down", disabled at the ends, plus a polite live region. Save sends the ids and shows "Saving…".
requirements: Each row is draggable. Dragging a row over another shows a drop indicator line above or below it (depending on which half the pointer is over); dropping moves the track there. The dragged row is faded while dragging
Each row has ▲ / ▼ buttons with aria-label="Move {title} up" / "… down", disabled on the first / last row. A visually hidden aria-live region announces "{title} moved to position 3 of 8"
A Save order button sends the current ids with savePlaylistOrder. While saving it reads "Saving…" and is disabled. Track numbers always show the current position
Reorder logic lives in one pure helper used by both drag and drop and the buttons; state is never mutated

change.title: Running time + unsaved changes
change.html:
"People build the playlist for a timed event. And they leave without saving."

  • The header shows the total: "Arvind · 8 songs · 30 min" (use formatTotal), and each row shows when it starts in the playlist: "starts 4:11". Both recalculate on every reorder.
  • Show "● Unsaved changes" while the order differs from the last saved order, and "✓ All changes saved" otherwise. Save is disabled when nothing changed. A Discard button restores the saved order.

Hint: keep savedIds (what the server has). "Dirty" is derived by comparing id lists. Moving a track and moving it back must be clean again.

hints: Search: "mdn html drag and drop api". You need draggable, onDragStart, onDragOver (call e.preventDefault()!), onDrop and onDragEnd.
In onDragStart call e.dataTransfer.setData("text/plain", id); Firefox will not start a drag without data.
Before / after: const rect = e.currentTarget.getBoundingClientRect(); const after = e.clientY > rect.top + rect.height / 2;
The helper: const next = [...list]; const [item] = next.splice(from, 1); next.splice(to, 0, item); return next;
Drop index: let to = indexOf(target); if (after) to += 1; if (from < to) to -= 1; (removing the dragged row shifts everything after it).
Start times: build an array above the return with a running total in a forEach, then read starts[i] in the map. Dirty: tracks.map((t) => t.id).join() !== savedIds.join().
rubric: One pure move helper shared by drag and buttons
dragover preventDefault and the index-shift edge case handled
Indicator state cleared on drop and on dragend (also when dropped outside)
Buttons are a real keyboard / screen reader alternative (labels, disabled ends, live region)
Save shows pending state; savedIds updated only after success
Totals, start times and dirty flag derived, not stored
Explained why not to keep index-based keys

notes: inset box-shadow 3px coral, top or bottom

dc44.title: Command palette (⌘K)
dc44.summary: A deploy dashboard already has every action as data. Build the Ctrl/Cmd+K palette: fuzzy filter, arrow keys, Enter to run, Escape, focus restore.
dc44.brief:
Orbit is a deploy dashboard. App.tsx has Sidebar, TopBar (with a "Search or run a command… ⌘K" button that does nothing yet), DeploymentList and App. Read commands.ts first: buildCommands(actions) already returns every action as { id, label, section, run }, and App already builds the list. components/Kbd.tsx renders key caps.

Your job is the palette itself. Each command's run() changes something visible (page, theme, sidebar, a queued deployment, a toast).

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4. Change: section headers (~24 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan · 7–24 Core · 24–31 change · 31–35 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"App owns paletteOpen, because both the shortcut and the top-bar button open it, plus a returnFocus ref with the element that had focus. The palette is its own component, only rendered while open, so its query and active index reset on every open. The filtered list is derived. Focus stays in the input the whole time; Arrow keys change active (wrapping), Enter runs results[active], Escape closes, and I wire aria-activedescendant so screen readers follow. When it closes, an effect puts focus back on the saved element."
requirements: Ctrl/Cmd+K anywhere (and clicking the top-bar search button) opens a centered palette over a dimmed backdrop with the input focused. Pressing it again, Escape, or clicking the backdrop closes it. The browser's own Ctrl+K is prevented
Typing filters commands fuzzy-ish: every typed letter must appear in order, case-insensitive, spaces ignored ("rdp" matches "Redeploy production"). Show "No commands match" when empty

↑ / ↓ move a highlighted item (wrapping at the ends, hover also highlights), Enter runs it and closes; clicking an item runs it too. The input has role="combobox" + aria-activedescendant; items are role="option" with aria-selected
When the palette closes, focus returns to the element that was focused before it opened (e.g. the sidebar link or the search button)

change.title: Group by section
change.html:
"With more commands coming, the flat list is hard to scan."

  • Show results grouped under section headers in this order: Navigation, Deployments, Appearance (SECTIONS in commands.ts). Hide a header when none of its commands match.
  • Arrow keys must follow the visual order across groups.

Hint: build one flat results array in section order and use it for both rendering and the active index.

hints: Global shortcut: document.addEventListener("keydown", ...) in an effect, with cleanup. if ((e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey) && e.key.toLowerCase() === "k") { e.preventDefault(); ... }
Fuzzy match: walk the query letters, each time pos = text.indexOf(ch, pos); if it is -1 return false, else pos += 1.
Reset active to 0 in the input's onChange, so a shorter list never leaves the highlight out of range.
Arrows: e.preventDefault() (otherwise the cursor jumps), then setActive((i) => (i + 1) % results.length). Search: "aria-activedescendant combobox mdn".
Focus restore: store e.target from the keydown (or the button from the click) in a ref when opening; useEffect(() => { if (!open && ref.current) { ref.current.focus(); } }, [open]);
Grouping: SECTIONS.forEach((s) => { commands.forEach((c) => { if (c.section === s && fuzzyMatch(c.label, query)) results.push(c); }); });
rubric: Open state in App; palette state local and reset by unmounting
Results derived; active index reset on query change
Keyboard handling with preventDefault where needed, wrapping
ARIA: combobox input, listbox / option, aria-activedescendant
Listener cleanup; no stale closure bugs on the toggle
Focus returns to the previous element
Grouping keeps keyboard order equal to visual order

notes: h 38 · radius 8 · active: panel-2 + 2px accent bar

dc45.title: Budget grid: editable cells
dc45.summary: Turn a read-only budget table into a small spreadsheet: click to edit, Enter/Tab to move, derived row and column totals, invalid input highlighted.
dc45.brief:
Ledgerly shows a quarterly budget. App.tsx has AppHeader, BudgetTable and App; getBudget() takes 0.4–1.0 s. Read utils/money.ts: formatMoney and parseAmount (returns null for text that is not a number) are there for you. utils/id.ts has uid.

Right now the cells are plain text. Make it behave like a tiny spreadsheet.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4. Change: add / delete rows (~24 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan · 7–24 Core · 24–31 change · 31–35 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"I'll store each cell as the text the user typed (cells: string[]), not a number. That way an invalid entry like "abc" stays visible and highlighted instead of being lost. Totals are derived with parseAmount, skipping invalid cells. Editing state is { row, col } | null plus a draft string; only one cell is an input at a time. Enter commits and moves down, Tab commits and moves right (wrapping to the next row), Shift+Tab goes back, Escape cancels, blur commits."
requirements: Clicking a cell turns it into a focused input with its current value. Enter saves and moves to the cell below (or stops editing on the last row). Escape cancels. Clicking elsewhere (blur) saves
Tab saves and moves right, wrapping to the first month of the next row; Shift+Tab moves left. Focus never leaves the grid while tabbing between cells
A Total column (per row) and a footer row of column totals plus a grand total, all derived and formatted with formatMoney

Input that is not a number (e.g. "abc") is kept and shown in a red-highlighted cell (title "Not a number"), left out of totals, and a message says "1 cell needs a number. They are left out of the totals." "1,000" and "$50" are valid

change.title: Add and delete rows
change.html:
"Finance wants to add a category for insurance, and drop advertising."

  • Under the table: a "New category" input and a + Add row button (disabled when empty). The new row has empty cells (counted as $0).
  • Each row gets a × button (aria-label="Delete {category}") at the end. All totals update.

Watch out: if you store the editing position by index, deleting a row shifts indexes. Stop editing when a row is deleted.

hints: Convert once on load: cells: r.values.map((v) => String(v)). Now "abc" can be stored.
Render: if (isEditing) return <td><input autoFocus ... /></td>; otherwise a <button> inside the td (keyboard-focusable for free).
One commit function: function commit(next: CellPos | null) { onCellChange(editing.row, editing.col, draft); if (next) startEdit(next.row, next.col); else setEditing(null); }
Tab: e.preventDefault() first, or the browser moves focus to the next button. Search: "mdn keydown Tab preventDefault".
Totals: cells.reduce((sum, t) => { const n = parseAmount(t); return n === null ? sum : sum + n; }, 0) (written with an if, of course).
rubric: Stored raw strings and explained why (invalid input stays visible)
Single editing position; draft separate from committed value
Enter / Tab / Shift+Tab / Escape / blur all behave as specified
Totals derived, invalid cells excluded
Immutable nested update of a single cell
Row add / delete with stable ids, editing cleared on delete
Accessible: real buttons and labelled inputs

notes: danger-soft bg · 1px danger ring · danger text
input h 34 w 200 · button h 34 brand

dc46.title: Theater seat picker
dc46.summary: Select up to 4 seats on a theater map, see a priced summary, book through the API, and recover when a seat gets taken mid-checkout.
dc46.brief:
Lumen Playhouse sells seats for Hamlet. App.tsx has ShowHeader, Legend, SeatGrid, Summary and App. getSeatMap() (0.4–1.0 s) returns every seat with its tier, price and taken flag. formatPrice is in utils/money.ts.

Read bookSeats in api.ts carefully: it takes 0.8–1.4 s and always rejects a booking that includes seat C5 (someone else grabbed it), which also marks C5 as taken on the server. That is how you test the failure path.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4. Change: keyboard-selectable seats (~26 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–8 plan · 8–26 Core · 26–34 change · 34–38 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"App owns selected: string[] (seat ids, in pick order), booking, and a message. The selected seat objects and the total are derived from the map. Toggle refuses taken seats and a 5th seat (with a notice). Book calls bookSeats(selected): on success show a confirmation and clear the selection; on failure show the error. Either way, refetch the map. I'll do that with a reloadKey state the load effect depends on, so there is one loading code path, and after each load I drop selected seats that are now taken."
requirements: Clicking an available seat selects it (gold, aria-pressed="true"); clicking again deselects. Taken seats can't be selected. A 5th seat is refused with the notice "You can select up to 4 seats."
The summary lists each selected seat ("C4 · Standard · $65" with a × remove button), the total by tier price, and the button reads "Book 2 seats · $160" (disabled with nothing selected)
Booking shows "Booking…" (disabled). Success: a banner "Booked! Confirmation LMN-… · seats A5, A6", selection cleared, and the refreshed map shows those seats taken
Failure (any booking with C5): an error banner with the API message, the map is refetched (C5 now taken) and C5 is removed from the selection while the other seats stay selected

change.title: Keyboard seat selection
change.html:
"Accessibility audit: the seat map is a wall of 60 tab stops."

  • Only one seat is in the Tab order (roving tabIndex). Arrow keys move focus between seats (also across taken seats, stopping at the edges). Enter / Space toggle the focused seat.
  • Each seat has aria-label="Row C, seat 5, Standard $65" (plus ", taken") and taken seats use aria-disabled so they stay reachable.

Search: "roving tabindex", "aria-disabled vs disabled".

hints: Derived: const selectedSeats = selected.map(id => map.seats.find(...)) and total = selectedSeats.reduce(...). Don't store the total.
Refetch pattern: const [reloadKey, setReloadKey] = useState(0); and the load effect has [reloadKey] deps. Bump it in .finally().
After the map loads: setSelected((prev) => prev.filter((id) => seat is not taken)).
Promise chain: bookSeats(ids).then(...).catch((err: Error) => { setError(err.message); }).finally(() => { setBooking(false); ... });
Roving tabindex: focusId state; tabIndex={s.id === focusId ? 0 : -1} (as an if above). Keep refs in useRef<Record<string, HTMLButtonElement | null>>({}) and call .focus() on arrow keys.
A <button> already fires onClick on Enter and Space, so you only handle arrows.
rubric: Selection limit enforced with clear feedback
Totals and labels derived from selected ids
Pending state prevents double booking
Failure path: error shown, map refetched, stale selection pruned
Single load path reused for refresh
Roving tabindex + arrow keys + aria labels
Talked about the real-world race (server is the source of truth)

notes: gold bg · dark text · 2px gold glow

dc47.title: Comment tree
dc47.summary: Render a forum thread's nested replies at any depth with a recursive component, collapse subtrees, and upvote optimistically with rollback.
dc47.brief:
Threadline is a discussion forum. App.tsx has PostHeader, CommentItem and App. getThread() (0.4–1.0 s) returns comments where each one has replies: Comment[], nested to any depth. Only the top level renders today.

upvoteComment(id, shouldFail) takes 0.4–0.9 s; the existing "Simulate offline" checkbox should be passed as shouldFail. Reuse utils/time.ts (timeAgo) and components/Avatar.tsx.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4. Change: sort by Top / New (~24 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–7 plan · 7–24 Core · 24–31 change · 31–35 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"A CommentNode renders one comment and then maps its replies to more CommentNodes: recursion handles any depth. Collapse is local state in each node, because it only affects that subtree. The hidden count is a recursive helper, countDescendants.

Votes I'll lift to App as a map { [id]: true } instead of editing the nested tree: the shown score is score + 1 if voted. Optimistic: set it immediately, call the API, and on failure delete the key and show an error. The map is passed down through the recursion."
requirements: All replies render at any depth with a recursive component; each level is indented with a thread line on the left

Each comment header has a [–] toggle (aria-expanded). Collapsing hides its text, actions and whole subtree, changes the toggle to [+], and shows "4 replies hidden" (all descendants, any depth; "1 reply hidden" for one)
Upvote (▲) increases the score immediately and disables the button (one vote per comment). The API is called in the background
With "Simulate offline" checked, the vote is rolled back when the request fails, the button is enabled again, and a message says the vote could not be saved

change.title: Sort by Top / New
change.html:
"Long threads bury new replies."

  • Add a Sort by select (Top / New) above the comments. Top = highest score first (including your vote); New = most recent first.
  • The sort applies to the top level and to the replies at every level. Collapsed state should survive re-sorting.

Hint: sort a copy ([...list].sort()), never the array from state. Stable keys keep each node's collapsed state.

hints: A component can render itself: inside CommentNode, comment.replies.map((r) => { return <CommentNode key={r.id} comment={r} ... />; }). The recursion stops when replies is empty.
Hidden count: function countDescendants(c) { return c.replies.reduce((sum, r) => sum + 1 + countDescendants(r), 0); }
Votes as a lookup instead of rewriting the tree: const [votes, setVotes] = useState<Record<string, boolean>>({});
Rollback: upvoteComment(id, offline).catch(() => { setVotes((prev) => { const next = { ...prev }; delete next[id]; return next; }); });. Search: "optimistic ui rollback react".
Sorting: [...list].sort((a, b) => displayScore(b) - displayScore(a)) for Top, a.minutesAgo - b.minutesAgo for New.
rubric: Recursive component with stable keys
Collapse kept local and explained why
Descendant count via recursion, derived
Votes lifted to App without mutating the nested tree
Optimistic update uses the updater form and rolls back on failure
Sorting copies arrays; applied at every depth
Mentioned deep trees / performance trade-offs (memo, flattening)

dc48.title: Mini form builder
dc48.summary: Build a no-code form editor: add, edit, reorder and delete fields, with a live preview that renders a working form and validates required fields.
dc48.brief:
Formcraft is a form builder. App.tsx has AddFieldPanel, FieldCard, PreviewPanel and App; getForm() loads two fields after 0.3–0.8 s. The type buttons do nothing yet, the cards are read-only, and the preview is a placeholder.

Read api.ts for the Field type, utils/fieldTypes.ts (FIELD_TYPES, typeInfo, isEmail), utils/id.ts and components/Toggle.tsx (use it for "Required").

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4. Change: JSON export panel (~28 min).

Timeline: 0–4 read · 4–8 plan · 8–28 Core · 28–35 Next + change · 35–40 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The field definitions live in App as Field[]; the builder and the preview both read them. I'll have one handleChange(id, patch) that merges a Partial<Field>, so label, required and options all share it. Add creates a field with a uid; move and delete are small immutable helpers.

The preview is a separate component with its own values and errors keyed by field id; it switches on field.type to render an input, select or checkbox. Submit validates every field and shows errors under each one, or a success message."
requirements: The 4 type buttons add a field at the end ("Untitled short text", "Untitled dropdown", …; dropdowns start with "Option 1" and "Option 2"). Each builder card has a label input, a Required toggle (reuse Toggle), and a ✕ delete button

The live preview renders a real form from the fields: text and email inputs, a select ("Choose…" plus options), a checkbox. Labels are linked to inputs; required fields show a red *. Changes in the builder show up immediately

Submit validates: empty required fields show "This field is required" (unchecked required checkbox: "Please check this box"), invalid email "Enter a valid email". Errors clear as the user fixes the field; a valid submit shows "✓ Submitted…"
Fields can be reordered with ↑ / ↓ buttons (disabled at the ends); dropdown cards have an "Options (one per line)" textarea; blank lines are ignored in the preview

change.title: Export as JSON
change.html:
"Engineering wants to paste the form definition into the backend config."

  • Below the preview add a read-only panel "Form definition (JSON)" showing { name, fields } pretty-printed with 2-space indentation.
  • It updates live as the form is edited.

One line of logic: JSON.stringify(value, null, 2) in a <pre>. It is derived, so no state.

hints: One update function: function handleChange(id: string, patch: Partial<Field>) { setFields((prev) => prev.map((f) => f.id === id ? { ...f, ...patch } : f)); } (write the ternary as an if).
Options textarea: value={field.options.join("\n")} and onChange={(e) => { onChange(field.id, { options: e.target.value.split("\n") }); }}.
Preview values: useState<Record<string, string | boolean>>({}); a checkbox stores a boolean, everything else a string.
Validate in submit: loop the fields, build an errors object, setErrors(errors). Use noValidate on the form so the browser doesn't show its own bubbles. Search: "mdn form novalidate".
Accessibility: <label htmlFor={id}>, aria-invalid and aria-describedby pointing at the error text.
rubric: Single source of truth for field definitions shared by builder and preview
Partial-update helper instead of one handler per property
Preview renders by type with linked labels
Validation computed on submit, errors keyed by id, cleared on edit
Reorder / delete immutable, stable ids as keys
JSON panel derived from state
Reused Toggle, FIELD_TYPES and isEmail from the codebase

dc49.title: Accessible country combobox
dc49.summary: Replace a native select with a fully accessible ARIA combobox: typing filters, full keyboard support, aria-activedescendant, clear button, then multi-select chips.
dc49.brief:
Passage is a visa application. Step 2 asks "Countries visited". App.tsx has Steps and App, and uses components/FormField.tsx for labels and hints (read it: the label points at the control via htmlFor). getCountries() returns 40 countries after 0.4–1.0 s. Today it's a native <select> that is painful with 40 options.

Build a CountryCombobox component (new file in components/) following the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern. This is a staff-level accessibility exercise: the details are the point.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4–5. Change: multi-select with removable chips (~30 min).

Timeline: 0–5 read · 5–9 plan · 9–30 Core · 30–40 change · 40–45 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Focus never leaves the input. The component owns query, open and the active index; the filtered options are derived. The input gets role="combobox", aria-expanded, aria-controls pointing at the listbox id, and aria-activedescendant pointing at the active option's id; that's how a screen reader follows the highlight without moving focus. Options get role="option" and aria-selected.

Keyboard in one onKeyDown: ↓/↑ open or move (clamped), Home/End jump, Enter selects, Escape closes (then clears), Tab closes and lets focus move. Options use onMouseDown preventDefault so clicking doesn't blur the input. The selected value is lifted to App via onChange, so the form can submit it. I'll scroll the active option into view in an effect."
requirements: A text input with role="combobox", aria-expanded, aria-controls (the listbox id), aria-autocomplete="list", linked to the "Countries visited" label and hint. The popup is a role="listbox" with role="option" children (flag + name) and unique ids. Disabled with "Loading countries…" until loaded
Typing filters options (case-insensitive "contains") and opens the list with the first option active; "No countries match" when empty. Clicking an option selects it (focus stays in the input)

Keyboard: ↓/↑ open the list or move the active option (clamped at the ends, scrolled into view), Home/End jump to first/last while open, Enter selects the active option (without submitting the form), Escape closes (a second Escape clears the text), Tab closes without selecting
aria-activedescendant always points at the highlighted option while open and is removed when closed; selected options have aria-selected="true" and a ✓
A ✕ clear button (aria-label) empties the value and returns focus to the input. Blur closes the list

change.title: Multi-select with chips
change.html:
"Applicants usually visited several countries."

  • Selecting adds the country as a chip inside the field (flag + name + × button with aria-label="Remove France"); the text clears and the list stays open for the next pick. Selecting an already-selected country removes it.
  • Backspace in the empty input removes the last chip. Removing a chip returns focus to the input. The listbox gets aria-multiselectable="true" and a polite live region announces "3 countries selected".
  • Save shows all selected names: "Countries: Japan, France".

hints: Read the pattern first. Search: "aria apg combobox list autocomplete" (w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg). Copy its attribute list, not its code.
Option ids must be unique on the page: id={inputId + "-opt-" + c.code}. Then aria-activedescendant={activeId} where activeId is undefined when closed.
Keep the active index valid when the list shrinks: const activeIndex = Math.min(active, options.length - 1); and reset to 0 on every keystroke.
Clicking an option blurs the input before the click fires. Fix: onMouseDown={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); }} on each option.
Scroll into view: useEffect(() => { listRef.current.children[activeIndex].scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" }); }, [activeIndex, open]); Search: "mdn scrollIntoView block nearest".
Enter: only preventDefault() when you actually select something; otherwise let Enter submit the form like any input.
rubric: All ARIA attributes correct and wired by id (combobox, listbox, option, activedescendant, expanded)
Focus stays in the input; mousedown preventDefault on options
Complete keyboard map including Home/End, Escape twice, Tab
Active option kept valid and scrolled into view
Value lifted to App; component reusable (props, no global ids)
Chips: remove buttons labelled, Backspace removal, focus returned, live region
Talked about screen reader testing (VoiceOver / NVDA) and the APG

notes: h 38 · radius 8 · active: primary-soft + 3px left bar

dc50.title: Virtualized log viewer
dc50.summary: Render 10,000 log lines smoothly by drawing only the visible rows (plus overscan) from scrollTop math, with a sticky header, filters, and jump-to-line.
dc50.brief:
Tracewell is a log explorer. getLogs() returns 10,000 lines after 0.8–1.5 s. Rendering them all freezes the tab, so the starter only shows the first 200. components/LogRow.tsx renders one row and the header, and exports ROW_HEIGHT (26px: every row is exactly that tall). formatNumber is in utils/format.ts.

Build virtualization by hand (no libraries): keep the scroll container's full height, but only render the rows that are on screen.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4. Change: jump to line (~30 min).

Timeline: 0–5 read · 5–9 plan · 9–30 Core · 30–40 change · 40–45 talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The scroller keeps its real height through a spacer div of count × ROW_HEIGHT, so the scrollbar is right. I track scrollTop from onScroll and the viewport height from a ResizeObserver. Then start = floor(scrollTop / H) - overscan, end = ceil((scrollTop + viewport) / H) + overscan, clamped, and I render only slice(start, end), each absolutely positioned at top: index × H.

The header is position: sticky inside the scroller. Filtering is a useMemo over level + text, and virtualization runs on the filtered list, so it stays fast. When the filter changes I reset the scroll to the top."
requirements: All 10,000 lines are scrollable but only the visible rows plus an overscan of ~8 above and below are in the DOM (fewer than ~90 rows at any time). The scrollbar reflects the full list (spacer height = rows × 26px)
Rows are positioned from scrollTop math (not by rendering everything); scrolling fast never shows blank gaps. Viewport height is measured (and re-measured on resize)
The column header stays visible (position: sticky) while scrolling

A text filter (message or service) and level buttons (ALL / DEBUG / INFO / WARN / ERROR) filter the list, virtualization keeps working on the filtered rows, the scroll resets to the top, and "1,234 / 10,000" shows the match count

change.title: Jump to line
change.html:
"Support pastes a line number from an alert and needs to see it."

  • Add a "Line #" input and a Go button. Go scrolls so that line is in the middle of the viewport and highlights it (accent background + left bar).
  • Errors: "Enter a line between 1 and 10,000" for invalid input, and "Line 42 is hidden by the current filter" when the line is filtered out.

The row may not be rendered yet, so you can't scrollIntoView it. Compute the scroll position from its index instead.

hints: Structure: <div className="log-scroll" ref onScroll> <LogHeader /> <div style={{ position: "relative", height: total }}>{visible rows}</div> </div>
Measure: const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => setViewportHeight(el.clientHeight)); ro.observe(el); and ro.disconnect() in cleanup. Search: "mdn ResizeObserver".
Window: const start = Math.max(0, Math.floor(scrollTop / ROW_HEIGHT) - OVERSCAN); const end = Math.min(rows.length, Math.ceil((scrollTop + viewportHeight) / ROW_HEIGHT) + OVERSCAN);
Each visible row: style={{ top: (start + i) * ROW_HEIGHT }} with position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0 in CSS. Key by line, not by i.
Wrap the filter in useMemo(() => ..., [logs, query, level]): onScroll re-renders often, and re-filtering 10,000 rows each time is wasteful.
Jump: const index = filtered.findIndex((l) => l.line === n); scrollRef.current.scrollTop = index * ROW_HEIGHT - (viewport - header) / 2;
rubric: Correct window math with overscan and clamping
Spacer keeps the true scroll height; rows absolutely positioned
Viewport measured with ResizeObserver, cleaned up
Filtering memoized; virtualization runs on the filtered list
Scroll reset on filter change explained
Jump computes position from index; validation messages
Discussed variable row heights and why libraries (react-window) exist

notes: input w 80 h 30 · Go button accent
